chapter: Instruments, tenors and the current band
title: His engraved Selmer alto, stolen and recovered
summary: One of two engraved Selmer altos, once owned by Rudy Vallee, was stolen several times; the State Department returned it after Morocco.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Uh-huh, very nice. Your -- I don't think we really did much on the alto, either.

Well, I have one of two altos that were built by the Selmer Company, and this is almost as though it am, maybe older, was Zion, maybe Olter, I don't really -- no one has ever really been able to pinpoint -- I guess it's a -- and I'm only guessing, maybe a 15 or 16 hundred point period in Selmer, Sumner, all saxophones.

So it had to be one of the early stages, because it was told to me, and I only speak with loose memory, there were two available, and one was owned by Rudy Valley and I through a secondhand or a thirdhand or a fourth hand development, wound up
And they are quite a lovely instrument, as far as outward appearance and so on. They were completely engraved from top to bottom and so on.
I had this one stolen from me for a period of many years, maybe two or three or four times.
And each time it returns like a bad penny.

It's amazing. The last serious time I lost it was in Africa. I was in Morocco. It disappeared somewhere, in an airport or something. And then maybe -- almost a year later, our State Department people in Washington called me and said they had found it.
